negative_findings: findings.md was NOT written: the subagent harness refused report .md files. Its content is in this output. Every script, CSV and PNG is in /home/user/nordic-quality-rank/research/orkla_foods/analysis/robust/.

Nominal HAC(4) significance is badly inflated. When x is replaced by an independent persistent AR(2) placebo, a nominal 5% test rejects 17% of the time (median over 1,046 regressions; range 7-31%). The honest 5% critical |t| is about 2.7 for d_margin and vol_proxy and about 2.95 for og and d_og.
In the screen, 912 of 1,968 tests (46%) have nominal p<0.05. After placebo calibration and BY, only 172 survive at q<0.10 (d_margin 10, og 85, d_og 55, vol_proxy 22).

No macro variable predicts d_margin 1-2 quarters ahead at FDR-controlled significance. 10y yield changes, packaging PPI, EC selling-price expectations, the price-cost gap and SE real-wage acceleration are sign-stable at h1 but fail BY.

Real-wage hypothesis. Margin change: fragile, zero before 2013 and episode-driven; spurious at rt_h0. Implied volume: no effect at any alignment. og and d_og: robustly negative, which is an inflation mirror (price), not demand.

Consumer confidence (Orkla-weighted, Nordic, Finans Norge, NIER) has no effect on d_margin at any alignment. The strong negative link with og and d_og disappears once same-quarter food CPI is controlled, and og Granger-causes confidence, not the reverse.

Policy-rate changes, the 10y yield level and FX (Orkla-weighted vs EUR, EURNOK, EURSEK) are spurious (persistence) or have no effect for d_margin. For d_og, FX is only a 4-quarter base effect that fails FDR.

Input-cost levels (food PPI, FAO food index in NOK/EUR/local currency, EU agri basket, Nordic power, EU gas, Brent in NOK) are fragile or spurious for d_margin. Without 2021Q3-2023Q4, food PPI's t falls from -5.2 to -1.5, and the agri/FAO/energy measures show sign-reversing Quandt-Andrews breaks around 2004-07.

The 2021Q3-2023Q4 episode dominates d_margin. Across the 135 HAC-significant rows, those 10 quarters supply a median 55% of the covariance. Without them the coefficient shrinks to 63% of its full-sample size, and only 50% of rows keep p<0.10.
The pre-2021 rolling correlations of cost variables with d_margin are only -0.25 to -0.5.

Linear trends are not the problem: 89-99% of significant rows survive a trend control. Persistence is the problem. In the screen, Spearman(|t|, AR1) is 0.39 for d_margin and og. Features with AR1>0.9 are 35% (d_margin) and 65% (og) of the top 20, against 14% of all features.
Non-overlapping checks (Q4-only and calendar-year averages) keep the sign for almost all significant rows. The y/y overlap inflates t-values but does not create the signs.
Base effects at h4 for d_og are mechanical, not structural: level variables lagged 4+ quarters co-move with og(t-4). Examples are food CPI yoy, real wages, FX and unemployment.
key_numbers: Screen: 200 core features x {coincident, rt h0, rt h1} x 4 targets = 1,968 tests (492 per target). Nominal p<0.05: 912 tests. BY q<0.10: 509 nominal, 172 after placebo calibration.
Decisive FDR family: one per target (screen plus battery-only tests), 610-612 tests each. Calibrated BY q<0.10: d_margin 11, og 98, d_og 43, vol_proxy 22.
Battery: 1,046 rows (61 candidates x 4 targets x up to 5 alignments). ROBUST 76, FRAGILE 347, SPURIOUS 126, NO_EFFECT 497.
Candidate x target pairs: 231. Best class: ROBUST 45 (d_margin 6, og 21, d_og 16, vol_proxy 2), FRAGILE 122, SPURIOUS 30, NO_EFFECT 34.
d_margin ROBUST rows by alignment: coincident 5, rt_h0 1, rt_h1 0, rt_h2 0, rt_h4 1 (GSCPI).
A-priori hypotheses (46 features, 205 rows per target). ROBUST rows: d_margin 1, og 24, d_og 10, vol_proxy 0.
Placebo size of the nominal 5% HAC(4) test: median 17%. Median 95% placebo |t|: d_margin 2.72, og 2.97, d_og 2.92, vol_proxy 2.71.
d_margin vs 10y yield change: -1.09pp per +1pp (NO), t -5.2; t -3.8 without both COVID and 2021-23.
d_margin vs EU packaging PPI: -0.15pp per 1pp, t -7.6 coincident and -5.8 using the previous quarter.
og vs food CPI ex VAT: pass-through +0.58pp per 1pp (t 9.4). Food PPI: +0.5pp per 1pp.
d_og vs food CPI ex VAT acceleration: +0.24pp per 1pp (t 6.1). Real-wage acceleration: -0.65pp per 1pp (t -5.2).
Share of HAC-significant rows that keep sign and p<0.10 without 2021Q3-2023Q4: d_margin 50%, og 58%, d_og 69%, vol_proxy 34%.
Median coefficient without 2021Q3-2023Q4 as a share of the full-sample coefficient: d_margin 0.63, og 0.63, d_og 0.95, vol_proxy 0.46.
Volume proxy (og minus w_food_cpi_xvat_yoy) vs reported 2022Q2-2026Q2 volume/mix: correlation 0.83, MAE 1.85pp, mean bias -0.35pp.

Quandt-Andrews slope break at 5%: 46-62% of HAC-significant rows. About a third reverse the sign, mostly with break dates in 2004-07 or 2020-23. 3 of the 7 ROBUST d_margin rows show a magnitude break at 2022Q3 (definition E).
caveats: Deliverables: robust_summary.csv (main table: classification, reasons, betas, p_cal, q-values, era signs, sub-samples, Chow and sup-Wald, leave-one-year-out, Q4/annual, rolling, trend, own-history and channel controls, Granger, check flags), robust_summary_by_pair.csv, top_predictors.csv, fdr_counts.csv, episode_dependence.csv, break_tests_summary.csv, fig_rolling_<target>.png, fig_subsamples_<target>.png, fig_apriori_class_grid.png, fig_placebo_size.png, fig_screen_persistence.png. Scripts 00-05 reproduce everything; 02_battery.py takes about 4 minutes, seed 20261006.

Classification rules. ROBUST = calibrated p<0.05, BY q<0.10 in the per-target family, all core checks pass and at most one soft check fails. Core checks: sign in at least 3 of 4 eras; without 2021Q3-23Q4 p<0.10; leave-one-year-out never flips the sign and max p<0.10; survives a linear trend; no sign-reversing Quandt-Andrews break. Soft checks: without COVID; annual or Q4 non-overlap; rolling sign stable in at least 80% of windows; pre/post 2013; own-history control; without both episodes.

SPURIOUS triggers: persistence (calibrated p>=0.10), trend, the estimate without the episode has the opposite sign, annual estimate has the opposite sign, or a mechanical link. FRAGILE subtypes: fdr_only, borderline_calibration, unstable. NO_EFFECT replaces the label NULL (to avoid NaN parsing).
Calibrated p-values assume AR(2) dynamics for x and a normal approximation scaled to the placebo 95th percentile. Empirical placebo p-values (400 draws) are also reported.

All tests are univariate with controls: definition dummies B-E, COVID dummy, a calendar-adjustment-aware Easter term, and the d_og definition-break flag. The only multivariate check is t_chan, a horse race against same-quarter food CPI (og, d_og) or food PPI (d_margin). Rankings may change in a multivariate model because the price block is highly collinear.
Era sub-samples are small (C is 7 quarters inside B/C; E is 16), so era betas are noisy and only their signs are used.
Macro data are the latest vintage. Real-time alignment handles publication lags, not revisions.
vol_proxy is an ex-post construction. It has a 2025 level bias (food CPI about 4% vs Orkla price about 1%). Food-CPI features are mechanically SPURIOUS for it.

ROBUST does not mean causal. Consumer confidence (og, d_og), price_wage_gap_d4 and SE confidence d4 (d_og) are robust proxies of the food-price channel. The policy-rate level (og) and 10y yield change (d_margin) are probably proxies of the nominal/cost cycle. GSCPI at h4 rests on the 2020-23 supply shock.
The og-to-food-price pass-through is regime-dependent. Rolling correlations were near 0 in the 2014-2020 low-inflation windows for headline and HICP-food measures.

common.py pitfall (not a bug, not modified): the india flag equals def_D plus 2007Q2-Q4. Using it together with the definition dummies creates an outlier dummy for 2007Q2-Q4 (margin changes -3.3, -2.8 and -1.75pp). I absorbed India in def_D and added an ex-India sub-sample instead. Also, og_r4 and d_og_r4 straddle definition breaks without a flag.

Organic growth 2001-05 is low precision (derived from year-to-date figures, rounded); quality weights are applied. Distribution deals counted as organic in 2015-16 and the 2013 Rieber basis add noise to eras B/C/D.
